name: an incoming request drives a profile card's stat and button to update live
looks: On a bright accent-colour field, a chat bubble with a short incoming request slides in above a small profile card. The card's headline stat rolls up through blurred digits to a higher percentage, a row of bars grows up beside it with the last bar in a contrasting colour, a status row ticks a render progress, and the card's main button swaps from a plain call-to-action to a filled, checked confirmation state.
build: data-infographic-style digit roll-up (digits slide under a vertical blur whose strength follows their speed) for the percentage, bars scaling up from a baseline with an uneven stagger; the card itself is a glass-ui-flow-style DOM group that springs in, with its button layer swapping fill colour/label and gaining a check icon on a short scale-pop (back.out) once the progress readout completes.
sound: A rising tone under the digit roll-up, soft blips on the bars, and a confirming chime as the button swaps to its done state.
prompt: On a bold colour field, have a short incoming message trigger a small profile or status card to update live: its headline number rolls up through blurred digits to a bigger figure, a bar chart grows beside it, a progress row ticks across, and the card's main button swaps into a filled, checked confirmation state, so the whole card feels like it is responding to the message in real time.
